name: Bypassed Rule
description: A push went around this ruleset rather than satisfying it. Distinct from BYPASSES, and the distinction is the point: BYPASSES is a standing permission (who MAY), this is an occurrence (who DID). Conflating them would make 'is permitted' and 'has actually done it' indistinguishable in a query, which is the whole value of the finding.

rule_type.description: The rule that was not satisfied (`required_status_checks`, `non_fast_forward`). One suite may bypass several rules of one ruleset; the edge carries the first, and the suite's `bypassed_rules` carries them all.

enforcement.description: The rule's enforcement at evaluation time (`active`, `evaluate`). An `evaluate` rule was never going to stop anything, so bypassing it means less.

details.description: GitHub's own explanation of the failure, verbatim (`Required status check "gate" is expected.`). Preserved rather than re-worded — it names the specific check.
